title: Frontdoor connection backlog: fast-fail shim, idempotency guard, and customer escalation runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
High-severity customer escalations reported intermittent 5xxs and long tail timeouts during short, high-concurrency bursts. Root cause analysis indicates a frontdoor connection/accept backlog (TCP/TLS accept queue growth combined with proxy worker saturation) which caused request queueing inside the proxy layer. Clients hit SDK retry loops that amplified traffic, producing cascading timeouts and 5xx responses for affected tenants.

Impact:
- Multiple customers reported elevated 5xx rates and tail latency spikes for ~10-30 minute windows during bursts.
- Failures are most visible for streaming and long-polling requests; also affected short requests when bursts coincide with TLS session churn.
- Amplification through client retries turned short blips into tenant-visible outages.

Root cause (so far):
- Frontdoor proxy has a limited accept/backlog depth on some kernel/hypervisor configs. Under TLS churn and many new connections per second, the accept queue grows and kernel drops/defers accepts, which stalls proxy worker threads.
- Proxy's current admission logic tries to be fair but does not fast-fail when internal request queueing exceeds safe thresholds.
- Clients retry aggressively without jitter or idempotency guidance; retries were often replayed into the same overloaded path.
- KV cache pressure and occasional kernel-level socket TIME_WAIT accumulation exacerbated the pressure.

Proposed mitigations (short-term hotfix and medium-term):
1) Hotpatch (Immediate) - frontdoor_fast_fail shim (feature-flagged):
   - Observe accept_queue_depth and proxy_inflight_queues. If either exceeds configured thresholds, return a stable 503 with Retry-After and a new header X-Redwood-FastFail-Reason to callers to prevent noisy retries.
   - Implement per-tenant soft admission: clients will receive a per-tenant cooldown header (X-Redwood-Cooldown: seconds) to signal SDKs to back off.
   - Deploy staged rollout to 10% frontdoor instances, monitor error rates/latency, then 100% if stable.
2) Idempotency guidance and SDK changes (Short term):
   - Add an SDK release that introduces jittered exponential backoff default and recommends idempotency keys for mutating operations.
   - Surface the new Retry-After and X-Redwood-Cooldown headers in SDK to respect server-side flow control.
3) Medium-term (runtime changes):
   - Improve proxy admission logic to prioritize short requests, avoid head-of-line blocking, and better manage TLS session reuse.
   - Socket/TCP tuning playbooks for private and dedicated deployments; upstream kernel knobs and envoy/proxy flags.
   - Add continuous sampling traces for requests that saw accept_queue delay to help root-cause future incidents.

Observability additions (required before full rollout):
- New metrics: frontdoor.accept_queue_depth, frontdoor.proxy_inflight_count, frontdoor.per_tenant_rejects, frontdoor.fast_fail_rate.
- New alert: sustained accept_queue_depth > threshold for 1m and fast_fail_rate > 0.5% => P1 alert to SRE.
- Dashboard: burst playback chart (request rate vs accept_queue vs 5xx rate) and tenant impact heatmap.

Runbook for customer escalation (for on-call/SEs):
1) If customers report elevated 5xxs, check frontdoor.accept_queue_depth and fast_fail_rate.
2) If fast_fail hotpatch is not enabled, enable feature-flag on subset of instances as mitigation and observe 10m window.
3) If specific tenant(s) dominate, apply per-tenant cooldown via control-plane API (temporary admission weight reduction).
4) Communicate: open an incident thread, post a preliminary status message to customer with recommended client-side SDK update (jittered retry) and estimated mitigation ETA.
5) After stabilization, schedule postmortem and plan medium-term fixes.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for fast-fail logic and header emissions.
- Integration test harness that simulates TLS churn and bursty new connections with controlled retries to validate sterilization of retry amplification.
- Canary rollout in staging with synthetic traffic and then in production with gradual rollout and strict abort conditions.

Rollback and safety gates:
- Feature-flag rollback path documented; removal by toggling flag via Console.
- Abort if tail latency increases by >10% or successful request rate drops for top 5 customers after 15m of rollout.

Customer communications:
- Drafted messages for SEs to send to escalated customers: acknowledgement, short description of mitigation (server-side backpressure + SDK guidance), recommended SDK patch, and ETA for permanent fix.
- Postmortem to include detailed timeline and recommended SDK defaults to reduce amplification (jitter, idempotency).

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/ENG-457221
- PR (hotpatch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontdoor/pull/5482
- Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/FRONTDOOR-RUNBOOK

2026-03-15 — Diego Ramos: Opened PR #5482 (hotpatch). Awaiting code review from H. Nguyen and QA signoff. Drafted customer message and runbook. Plan to canary to 10% at 2026-03-16 03:00 UTC.
